title: A New Hope in Yathrib
subtitle: The Encounters at Mina and the Dawn of Faith in Madinah
summary: The war-weary oasis of Yathrib, the strife between Aws and Khazraj, the prophetic outreach during pilgrimage seasons, the historic meeting at Aqabah with six men of Khazraj, their immediate acceptance of Islam, and the dawn of a transformative future.

sections.text: The Fractured Oasis of the North

Approximately two hundred and fifty miles north of Makkah lay the lush, date-palm oasis of Yathrib. Unlike the arid mercantile center of Makkah, Yathrib was an agrarian society blessed with subterranean springs, fertile volcanic soil, and expansive groves. Yet beneath its natural bounty, the city was trapped in a tragic cycle of tribal bloodshed. For generations, its two dominant Arab clans—the Aws and the Khazraj—had fought bitter wars of vengeance, culminating in the horrific Battle of Bu'ath barely a few years earlier, which had decimated the nobility on both sides and left the community exhausted, leaderless, and longing for peace.

Alongside the Arab tribes dwelt several prominent Jewish communities, including Banu Qaynuqa, Banu al-Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah. Possessing divine scriptures and learned traditions, the Jewish elders frequently rebuked their pagan neighbors during disputes, warning them: 'A prophet will soon be sent whose time is at hand; we shall follow him and slay you alongside him as the people of Aad and Iram were slain.' Through these constant warnings, the people of Yathrib grew uniquely familiar with monotheistic concepts, prophecy, and the expectation of divine revelation.
The fertile oasis landscape and distant palms of Yathrib where hope was reborn.
The Prophetic Outreach at the Pilgrimage Fairs

In Makkah, following the loss of Abu Talib's protection, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ adopted a systematic approach to present his message to the wider Arabian Peninsula. During the annual pilgrimage seasons and bustling trade fairs at Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz, when tribes gathered from across Arabia under sacred truces, the Prophet visited their encampments one by one. With indefatigable patience, he would stand before their tents, proclaim the oneness of God, and ask them to provide him sanctuary so that he could convey the divine message.

These efforts were met with constant hostility and betrayal. His bitter uncle Abu Lahab trailed his footsteps relentlessly, wearing fine clothes and shouting to the visiting tribesmen: 'O people, do not obey him! He is an apostate and a liar who wishes to sever your allegiance to your idols!' Tribe after tribe—Banu Amir, Banu Kalb, Banu Hanifah, and Kindah—rejected his appeal, either through fear of offending Quraysh or by demanding that political succession be granted to them after his victory. Yet the Prophet remained serene and steadfast, trusting in God's decree.

In the eleventh year of Prophethood (620 CE), during the pilgrimage season, the Prophet ﷺ walked through the defiles of Mina near the steep hillock known as Al-Aqabah. Hearing voices conversing by night, he approached a group of six travelers who were shaving their heads in completion of their pilgrimage rites. He greeted them warmly and asked: 'Who are you?' They replied: 'A group from the Khazraj.'

The Prophet inquired: 'Allies of the Jews?' They affirmed that they were. He then asked with his characteristic gentleness: 'Will you not sit with me so that I may speak with you?' They agreed, and the Prophet sat beside their fire. He explained the core message of Islam, called them to worship God alone, and recited verses from the Holy Quran. Classical chroniclers record that the six men included As'ad ibn Zurarah, Awf ibn al-Harith, Rafi' ibn Malik, Qutbah ibn Amir, Uqbah ibn Amir, and Jabir ibn Abdillah ibn Ri'ab.
The quiet night defiles of Mina where six seekers of truth listened to the divine recitation.
The Awakening of Faith and the Vow

As the majestic words of the Quran filled the cool desert air, the men of Yathrib looked at one another in profound astonishment. The memory of their Jewish neighbors' warnings instantly flashed through their minds. They whispered among themselves: 'By God, you know well that this is indeed the very prophet with whom the Jews have been threatening you! Let them not precede you to him!'

Without hesitation, all six men embraced Islam, declaring their testimony of faith before the Messenger of God. They said to him with heartfelt honesty: 'We have left our people behind in a state of discord and enmity like no other folk; perhaps God will unite them through you! We shall return to them, call them to your cause, and present to them this religion which we have accepted. If God unites them around you, then no man will be mightier than you!'

فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَتَلَا عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنَ قَالُوا: إِنَّا قَدْ تَرَكْنَا قَوْمَنَا، وَلَا قَوْمَ بَيْنَهُمْ مِنَ الْعَدَاوَةِ وَالشَّرِّ مَا بَيْنَهُمْ، فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْمَعَهُمْ بِكَ
'When the Messenger of God spoke to them and recited the Quran, they said: We have left our people with none having more enmity between them than they; perhaps God will unite them through you.' (Sirat Ibn Hisham)

The six men returned to Yathrib carrying the spark of divine revelation in their hearts. In every home, assembly, and date grove, they recounted the wondrous encounter at Aqabah, reciting the verses they had memorized. Within months, the mention of Muhammad ﷺ and the message of Islam became a common subject in Yathrib, ahead of the pledge that followed at al-Aqabah.
